title: The Escarpment of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Tamsin Delacroix, the last riverboat captain willing to run Patagonia's dry-side escarpment, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise: deliver it to his estranged daughter before the mining concession expires. The daughter turns out to be traveling under a false name, fleeing a judge who wants her testimony buried, and the map marks water rights that could bankrupt the company bankrolling both of them. Hunted by hired gauchos and betrayed by her own first mate, Tamsin must choose between the law that would protect her boat and the justice the wilderness demands. She runs the escarpment one final time, exposes the concession fraud at the land office in Puerto Deseado, and gives the inheritance to the daughter — who chooses to stay on the river as Tamsin's new pilot.
about_author: Gideon Almeida is the pen name of a former merchant-marine officer who spent six seasons running supply boats along the Patagonian coast before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people whose moral compasses are truer than their maps.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Fare
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A bloodied prospector boards her boat at a lonely dock, pays with a hand-drawn map, and makes her swear to find 'the girl with two names' before the season ends. He dies by morning. The emotional beat is reluctant obligation — Tamsin resents promises but honors them.

chapters.title: Two Names in Puerto Deseado
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In port she tracks down Elena Vasquez, a quiet cartographer who flinches at her own surname. Tamsin recognizes the dead man's eyes in her face but says nothing yet. Beat: suspicion sharpening into curiosity as Tamsin tests her with questions about rivers she shouldn't know.

chapters.title: The Company's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. A representative of Andes Sur Mining offers Elena money for 'her father's papers,' revealing he knows more than he should — and that her father was murdered, not drowned. Beat: fear curdling into resolve; Elena realizes the map is worth killing for.

chapters.title: Loading the Cazadora
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin hires Elena as deckhand to keep her close, hiding the map inside the ballast. Her first mate, Raul, notices the extra fuel drums and asks too many questions. Beat: uneasy partnership forming between two women each concealing half the truth.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Two gauchos board at a fuel stop demanding the prospector's effects; Tamsin strands them on a shoal by faking engine trouble. Beat: grim satisfaction — Tamsin discovers she enjoys fighting back outside the law's reach, and Elena sees who she really signed on with.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. A storm forces them ashore; Elena finds the map and reads it properly — it records an unregistered spring feeding three estancias the company has already bought through fraud. Beat: grief and fury; the inheritance isn't gold, it's proof.

chapters.title: Raul's Price
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Raul sells their position to the company for debt forgiveness and sabotages the radio. The gauchos ambush them at the Chacabuco narrows; Tamsin is shot in the shoulder running the rapids blind. Beat: betrayal and sacrifice — the boat barely survives, trust does not.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Run
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Wounded, feverish, Tamsin pilots the damaged Cazadora down the dry side's worst channel at night to outrun the company's launch, navigating from memory because the charts are gone. Beat: transcendent focus — the river forgives nothing, and tonight it doesn't have to.

chapters.title: Concession Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach Puerto Deseado hours before the permits expire; Elena files the spring survey and her father's affidavit with the land office while Tamsin holds off Raul and the company men at the dock. Beat: cathartic confrontation — justice delivered by paperwork and nerve, not guns.

chapters.title: Water Remembering
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The concession collapses; the estancia families get their water rights. Elena declines the money, asks instead to learn the sandbars. On the last page they cast off together, Tamsin finally telling someone what the dying man found. Beat: earned peace — inheritance passed, identity chosen.
